scope: Uniform consequences of the completed Appendix B compactness and bounded-set topology results; no additional unproved source clause is claimed.
results: On a specified original endpoint norm ball, finitely many original Fourier coefficient tests with one positive tolerance control any admissible lower finite-p norm, uniformly for every pair of potentials in the ball.

Uniform convergence of each original Fourier coefficient is equivalent to uniform convergence in every admissible lower finite-p norm, for families with a common endpoint norm bound. The testing set, family parameter and convergence filter are arbitrary; continuity in the testing parameter is not assumed.
The uniform convergence criterion still holds with only an eventual common endpoint bound for the approximating family, with the bound also imposed on the proposed limit family.

For nontrivial filters, uniform coefficient limits of eventually endpoint-bounded families uniquely recover a family of original physical endpoint potentials with the same specified bound and all reality, zero-mean and physical period-one constraints. One recovered family converges uniformly in every admissible lower norm and pointwise weak-star.
For 0<=r<1/2 the finite Fourier control and uniform convergence equivalence specialize to the norm of the identical original H-minus-one distributions.
qualifications: The endpoint bound uses the exact original FourierLebesgueSpace(2,-r,infinity) norm. No substituted coefficient norm or frequency convention is used.
All fixed lower exponents retain finite p>=1 and the strict threshold 1<(-r-t)*p.toReal.
Uniform convergence is tested separately for each Fourier mode. A finite set of modes is selected after the requested lower-norm tolerance, before the potentials.
The eventual bound holds for all testing parameters on one common eventual set. Separate parameter-dependent eventual bounds are not asserted to suffice.
The theorem constructing the limit requires a nontrivial filter. The equivalence theorems allow arbitrary filters.
No endpoint norm convergence, metrizability of the full unbounded weak-star space, actual KdV/Birkhoff construction or missing isospectral bound is inferred.
